key_origin.mechanism: Each encrypted UPD envelope names an RSA-2048 recipient key. The public sonostool implementation validates one recovery layout for its hardcoded SONOS_MODEL 26 target: an RSA blob in an MDP3 flash region (0x4000 bytes) at offset 0x0780, encrypted with an AES key derived as SHA256(OTP[0xD0:0xE0])[:16] from a 0x100-byte OTP/eFUSE dump. That storage layout has not been established for every other package model and must not be generalized without model-specific evidence.
key_origin.needed_per_model: Decrypting a package requires the private key matching its envelope recipient. For a model verified to use the sonostool MDP3 design, recovery requires the matching device's 16 KiB MDP and 256-byte OTP dump plus sufficient access to read them. Other hardware generations may store or derive the key differently. Device dumps contain secrets: never commit them; supply them out-of-band and retain only recipient fingerprints and component hashes.
key_origin.public_paths: Fenway model-8 family (MPC8314, includes Play:1): UART + diagnostic firmware gives root shell; mdputil reads flash; public dumps exist (trulyspinach/sonos-fenway) - origin of the model-8 key. Amlogic-era models (Sonos One and siblings): public EL3 exploit dumps OTP/eFUSE and sonostool derives MDP/LUKS/OTA keys without a device oracle (blasty/sonos, HITB Amsterdam 2023); requires the physical device and the exploit chain. Sonos One Gen 2 (Amlogic A113): published PCIe DMA attack yields root shell and cleartext firmware (Synacktiv, 2021). Sonos One / Era 100: OTA remote kernel exploitation and secure-boot chain research (NCC Group, BlackHat USA 2024).
key_origin.searched_2026_09_03: No published private keys were found for the then-missing recipients (checked: Fenway repo is model-8 only; trulyspinach/sonor has public Sub Gen1 MTD dumps but its published sample contains only MDP1 and no MDP3/model-private-key field; blasty/sonos ships tooling, not keys; systemcrash/sonos-firmware ships packages/manifests only). Recovery requires model-specific evidence and access to matching hardware or another verified key source.
key_origin.local_status_2026_09_09: Five recipient keys have now been recovered for package models 8, 9, 12, 16, and 17. All five are reproducible from encrypted wrappers in their plaintext 34.16-37101 updater binaries. Private keys and exact recovery intermediates are retained in the local gitignored recovery-work vault and never enter Git; its integrity can be checked with scripts/audit_recovery_vault.py. Twenty-eight recipient groups remain missing.

note: RSA recipient identifiers are SHA-1 hashes of the SPKI representation embedded in Sonos UPD envelopes. Private keys are deliberately not committed.
